Accumulate along an axis

Source: R/cumulative.R
rray-cumulative.Rd

  • rray_cumulative_all() checks if all values are TRUE so far along axis.

  • rray_cumulative_any() checks if any value is TRUE so far along axis.

  • rray_cumulative_max() computes the maximum so far along axis.

  • rray_cumulative_min() computes the minimum so far along axis.

  • rray_cumulative_prod() computes the product so far along axis.

  • rray_cumulative_sum() computes the sum so far along axis.

Usage

rray_cumulative_all(x, ..., axis)

rray_cumulative_any(x, ..., axis)

rray_cumulative_max(x, ..., axis)

rray_cumulative_min(x, ..., axis)

rray_cumulative_prod(x, ..., axis)

rray_cumulative_sum(x, ..., axis)

Arguments

x

An array.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

axis

A single integer. The axis to accumulate along. 1 accumulates down rows, 2 accumulates across columns, and so on.

Value

An array with the same dimensions and names as x.

Details

Each position along axis summarizes every position up to and including it.

All / Any

x must be logical. Missing values follow all() and any(), so a later FALSE or TRUE can settle an earlier NA:

rray_cumulative_all(c(TRUE, NA, FALSE), axis = 1L) # TRUE, NA, FALSE
rray_cumulative_any(c(FALSE, NA, TRUE), axis = 1L) # FALSE, NA, TRUE

Min / Max

x must be logical, integer, or double, and the result keeps the type of x. Once a line hits NA or NaN, the rest of it stays missing. A later NA replaces an earlier NaN, like max() and min():

rray_cumulative_max(c(1, NaN, 2, NA, 3), axis = 1L) # 1, NaN, NaN, NA, NA

For logical x, a later TRUE or FALSE does not settle an earlier NA, unlike rray_cumulative_any() and rray_cumulative_all():

rray_cumulative_max(c(NA, TRUE), axis = 1L) # NA, NA
rray_cumulative_any(c(NA, TRUE), axis = 1L) # NA, TRUE

Product

x must be logical, integer, double, or complex. Logicals and integers are cast to double.

When NA and NaN are both present, you get one of them, but which one depends on the platform and the order of the values. Either way, is.na() is TRUE from that point on:

rray_cumulative_prod(c(2, NA, NaN), axis = 1L) # 2, NA, NA or NaN

Sum

x must be logical, integer, double, or complex. Logicals are cast to integer.

An integer sum errors as soon as a running total overflows, even if a later value would bring it back in range. This differs from rray_sum(), which only checks the final total:

x <- c(.Machine$integer.max, 1L, -1L)
rray_sum(x, axes = 1L) # .Machine$integer.max
rray_cumulative_sum(x, axis = 1L) # Error

Once a line is NA, it stays NA, and a later overflow does not error.

When NA and NaN are both present, you get one of them, but which one depends on the platform and the order of the values. Either way, is.na() is TRUE from that point on:

rray_cumulative_sum(c(2, NA, NaN), axis = 1L) # 2, NA, NA or NaN

Examples

x <- array(c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, NA, TRUE), c(2L, 3L))
x
#>      [,1]  [,2] [,3]
#> [1,] TRUE FALSE   NA
#> [2,] TRUE  TRUE TRUE

# Down rows
rray_cumulative_all(x, axis = 1L)
#>      [,1]  [,2] [,3]
#> [1,] TRUE FALSE   NA
#> [2,] TRUE FALSE   NA
rray_cumulative_any(x, axis = 1L)
#>      [,1]  [,2] [,3]
#> [1,] TRUE FALSE   NA
#> [2,] TRUE  TRUE TRUE

# Across columns
rray_cumulative_all(x, axis = 2L)
#>      [,1]  [,2]  [,3]
#> [1,] TRUE FALSE FALSE
#> [2,] TRUE  TRUE  TRUE
rray_cumulative_any(x, axis = 2L)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE
#> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE

x <- array(c(3L, 1L, 2L, 5L, 4L, 0L), c(2L, 3L))
x
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    3    2    4
#> [2,]    1    5    0

# Running maximum and minimum across columns
rray_cumulative_max(x, axis = 2L)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    3    3    4
#> [2,]    1    5    5
rray_cumulative_min(x, axis = 2L)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    3    2    2
#> [2,]    1    1    0

# Running product down rows
rray_cumulative_prod(x, axis = 1L)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    3    2    4
#> [2,]    3   10    0

# Running sum across columns
rray_cumulative_sum(x, axis = 2L)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    3    5    9
#> [2,]    1    6    6
